chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim ibn Natana (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us from his father Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Yahya ibn Imran al-Halabi, from al-Harith ibn al-Mughira al-Nasri, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) say:

Whoever says "Glory be to God, and praise be to God, and there is no god but God, and God is the greatest" forty times after every obligatory prayer before moving his legs, and then asks God, he will be given what he asked for.

key_terms.الحمد لله: Alhamdulillah -- "Praise be to God": expression of gratitude and acknowledgment of God's blessings
key_terms.الله أكبر: Allahu Akbar -- "God is the greatest": declaration of God's supreme greatness
key_terms.دبر كل صلاة فريضة: After every obligatory prayer: refers to the ta'qibat period immediately following the salat
key_terms.سبحان الله: Subhan Allah -- "Glory be to God": declaration of God's transcendence above all imperfection
key_terms.لا إله إلا الله: La ilaha illallah -- "There is no god but God": the declaration of divine unity (tawhid)
key_terms.يثني رجليه: Before bending/moving his legs: indicates remaining in the prayer position

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for saying subhanallah, alhamdulillah, la ilaha illallah, and Allahu akbar forty times after each obligatory prayer?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) teaches that reciting the four praises (tasbih, tahmid, tahlil, takbir) forty times immediately after each obligatory prayer -- before even shifting one's sitting position -- and then making supplication, guarantees that the supplication will be answered. This practice, known as ta'qibat (post-prayer devotions), was emphasized by the Imams as a prime moment when prayers are accepted, as the worshipper is still in a state of spiritual connection from the obligatory prayer.
word_analysis: may God have mercy on him
